paper.title_en: Cosmological Constraints and Bayesian Evidence for Coupled $\phi$CDM with DESI DR2 Observations
paper.abstract_en:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We investigate a coupled $\phi$CDM cosmological model in which energy exchange between dark energy and dark matter is governed by the derivative interaction term $Q = 3\alpha \dot{\rho}_m$. We constrain the model using baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from DESI Data Release~2, combined with compressed CMB likelihoods and  Type~Ia supernova datasets, including Pantheon$^{+}$, DES-Dovekie, and Union3. Parameter estimation is performed via Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods, and Bayesian evidence is used for model comparison with $\Lambda$CDM. We find that the interaction parameter $\alpha$ is tightly constrained at the $\mathcal{O}(10^{-4})$ level and remains consistent with zero within $1\sigma$ across all dataset combinations, indicating no statistically significant evidence for dark sector interaction. The dark energy equation-of-state parameter remains close to $w_{\phi}=-1$, with only mild and statistically insignificant deviations toward a quintessence-like regime. While the inferred Hubble parameter shows a slight shift to higher values relative to $\Lambda$CDM, it remains insufficient to resolve the $H_0$ tension. The matter density parameter is consistent between both models within uncertainties. Bayesian model comparison consistently favors the $\Lambda$CDM model, with evidence ranging from moderate to strong depending on the dataset combination. Overall, the \textcolor{red}{coupled} $\phi$CDM model does not provide a significant improvement over the standard cosmological scenario in light of current observations.</jats:p>
